title: Welcome to the Web
description: Orientation: what frontend development is, how the client-server model works, what happens between a click and a rendered page, and how Forge's Learn/Practice/Grow loop works.

title: Developer Tools
description: Hands-on fluency with the browser's built-in DevTools: Elements, Console, Network, and a first guided debugging session combining all three.

title: HTML Fundamentals
description: Real, valid, semantic HTML from scratch: document structure, text, links, images, lists, tables, forms, and semantic regions, ending in a capstone page.

title: CSS Fundamentals
description: Styling and layout fundamentals: selectors, the cascade, the box model, spacing and typography, colors, display, Flexbox, Grid, and responsive design, ending in a capstone responsive interface.

title: JavaScript Fundamentals
description: Real programming logic: variables, data types and operators, conditionals, loops, functions, arrays, and objects, ending in a mini project combining all of it.

title: Browser and Debugging Fundamentals
description: How a browser turns HTML/CSS/JS into pixels, how to read a JavaScript error and its stack trace, console debugging, and two guided debugging challenges.

title: Advanced CSS and UI Engineering
description: Production-grade CSS: advanced Flexbox/Grid, positioning and stacking, performant transitions and animations, CSS architecture, and design tokens.

title: Modern JavaScript
description: ES6+ JavaScript for real applications: destructuring, spread/rest, template literals, modules, closures, scope, `this`, and asynchronous JavaScript with Promises and async/await.

title: Git and GitHub
description: Real version control workflow: commits, branches, merges, resolving conflicts, pull requests, and collaborating on a shared repository.

title: APIs and Web Data
description: Fetching, sending, and handling real data over HTTP: fetch/JSON, REST conventions, error handling, loading states, and authentication basics.

title: TypeScript Fundamentals
description: Adding static types to JavaScript: basic types, interfaces, typing functions, union types and narrowing, generics, and typing real-world data, ending in a capstone JS-to-TS conversion.

title: React Foundations
description: Component-based UI from the ground up: JSX, props, component composition, and the mental model that underlies every React application.

title: React Interaction and Effects
description: Making React apps interactive: state with useState, event handling, and synchronizing with the outside world using useEffect.

title: Component Architecture
description: Structuring real React applications: component composition, lifting state up, prop drilling and its alternatives, and reusable component design.

title: Routing and Application Structure
description: Multi-page React applications: client-side routing, nested routes, route parameters, and organizing a growing application's structure.

title: State Management
description: Managing state beyond a single component: Context, common state-management patterns, and when local state genuinely isn't enough.

title: Data Flow and Application Data
description: Data fetching patterns in React applications: loading/error states, caching, synchronizing server data with UI, and avoiding common data-flow bugs.

title: Testing
description: Testing frontend code with confidence: unit tests, component tests, mocking, and testing user interactions rather than implementation details.

title: Accessibility
description: Building interfaces that genuinely work for everyone: semantic HTML, ARIA, keyboard navigation, screen reader testing, and manual accessibility auditing.

title: Performance and Resilience
description: Making applications fast and resilient: rendering performance, bundle size, lazy loading, error boundaries, and graceful failure.

title: Frontend Security
description: Why frontend security matters, XSS and input sanitization, CSRF and the same-origin policy, CORS in practice, and authentication/token storage patterns.

title: Frontend Architecture
description: Architecting large-scale frontend applications: module boundaries, folder structure, scalability trade-offs, and architecture review practices.

title: Advanced React Patterns
description: Professional-level React patterns: compound components, render props, custom hooks, and performance optimization techniques.

title: Debugging Mastery
description: Professional-level debugging: complex bug hunts, performance profiling, and systematic root-cause analysis under realistic constraints.

title: Frontend Interview Engineering
description: Interview-specific preparation: whiteboard-style frontend problems, system design for frontend, and behavioral/technical interview practice.

title: Professional Portfolio Projects
description: Capstone-level portfolio projects that demonstrate professional frontend engineering judgment end to end.

title: Meta-Frameworks
description: Building with a modern meta-framework: app router fundamentals, server vs. client components, data fetching, API routes, rendering strategy, and deployment.
